description: Original internal adversaries for the Vampire, Harmonic Mutant, and Shapechanger subgroup catalogs. Each adversary is a corrupted reflection, ideological schism, predatory offshoot, or hostile inheritance arising from the subgroup's own themes. These are Continuum-original organizations and do not reproduce proprietary faction names or published text.

crowned-blood.name: The Crownless Regency
crowned-blood.classification: Puppet sovereigns and dispossessed court officers
crowned-blood.description: Former seneschals, regents, hereditary advisers, and dethroned elders who concluded that visible rulers are liabilities. They govern through replaceable princes, enthralled boards, forged succession records, and crises designed to prove that every domain requires their hidden hand.
crowned-blood.method: They undermine legitimate authority, install dependent figureheads, and preserve emergency powers long after the emergency has passed.
crowned-blood.conflict: The Crowned Blood sees rulership as a burden that must be justified. The Regency sees rulers as masks worn by whoever controls the room behind the throne.

ash-rebellion.name: The Red Committee
ash-rebellion.description: Insurgent vampires who discovered that revolution can become its own throne. They maintain endless states of emergency, accuse every compromise of betrayal, and feed upon the fear generated by internal purges conducted in the name of liberation.
ash-rebellion.method: They infiltrate resistance movements, manufacture traitors, and ensure no victory becomes stable enough to make their authority unnecessary.
ash-rebellion.conflict: The Ash Rebellion fights hierarchy so people can choose. The Red Committee destroys choice to ensure the revolution never ends.

velvet-fixation.name: The Pallid Salon
velvet-fixation.description: Collectors who no longer create, love, or even properly appreciate beauty. They drain inspiration from artists, preserve people as living exhibits, and destroy any work they cannot own, classify, or reproduce under their patronage.
velvet-fixation.method: They acquire studios, careers, lovers, memories, and audiences until the artist remains alive but no longer possesses an independent desire.
velvet-fixation.conflict: The Velvet Fixation risks obsession in pursuit of beauty. The Pallid Salon believes beauty exists only after it has been deprived of freedom.

fractured-moon.name: The Straight Line
fractured-moon.description: Seers who regard uncertainty as failure and contradiction as treason. Rather than interpret visions, they remove inconvenient witnesses, force symbolic events into literal form, and prune possible futures until their preferred prophecy appears inevitable.
fractured-moon.method: They stage omens, manipulate succession, and kill alternate interpretations before those interpretations can gather believers.
fractured-moon.conflict: The Fractured Moon survives by accepting useful truth inside uncertainty. The Straight Line turns foresight into a weapon against every future it did not predict.

beast-remnant.name: The Kennel of Glass
beast-remnant.description: A network of handlers, laboratories, and domesticated elders that captures feral or isolated vampires and rebuilds them as disciplined hunting assets. Their subjects retain sharpened senses but lose the right to decide what deserves pursuit.
beast-remnant.method: They use blood conditioning, sensory deprivation, reward cycles, and corporate deployment contracts to turn instinct into obedience.
beast-remnant.conflict: The Beast Remnant struggles to live with predatory instinct. The Kennel of Glass treats instinct as property belonging to whoever holds the leash.

underveil-kin.name: The Lit Warrens
underveil-kin.description: Hidden kin who survived by selling the hidden routes, faces, shelters, and weaknesses of their own communities to courts, hunters, landlords, and security interests. They do not expose the entire underworld; they illuminate one rival tunnel at a time.
underveil-kin.method: They trade maps, maintenance access, sensor gaps, burial sites, and refugee identities for status in institutions that will never truly accept them.
underveil-kin.conflict: The Underveil Kin preserve life beneath official notice. The Lit Warrens monetize that concealment by deciding whose darkness is sold.

crimson-calculists.name: The Empty Formulae
crimson-calculists.description: Occult researchers who abandoned the idea that a living subject has moral standing once reduced to a variable. They test rites on captives, convert feeding populations into datasets, and treat every curse as an optimization problem with disposable inputs.
crimson-calculists.method: They acquire clinics, donor registries, prisons, and continuity laboratories where suffering can be hidden inside procedure.
crimson-calculists.conflict: The Crimson Calculists seek repeatable understanding. The Empty Formulae remove every ethical limit that prevents knowledge from becoming industrial predation.

starless-court.name: The Noon Throne
starless-court.description: Shadow sovereigns who decided secrecy is cowardice. They use spectacle, public fear, staged daylight survivals, and impossible broadcasts to prove that authority belongs to the predator willing to be seen and remain unpunished.
starless-court.method: They expose selected supernatural acts, then control the panic, investigation, and retaliation those revelations create.
starless-court.conflict: The Starless Court uses darkness as political territory. The Noon Throne seeks legitimacy through unavoidable public terror.

sepulcher-choir.name: The Borrowed Dead
sepulcher-choir.description: Death brokers who steal final memories, imitate ancestral voices, and manufacture testimony from bodies that can no longer challenge the interpretation. Entire inheritances and wars have begun because the Borrowed Dead made a corpse say what the living needed to hear.
sepulcher-choir.method: They traffic in remains, death sites, funerary access, and reconstructed last words tailored to the buyer.
sepulcher-choir.conflict: The Sepulcher Choir treats the dead as a political constituency. The Borrowed Dead treats them as evidence that cannot object.

quiet-tribunal.name: The Red Appeal
quiet-tribunal.description: Former judges and sanctioned hunters who learned that a sentence can justify feeding, confiscation, and political removal. They construct crimes backward from the punishment desired and call every surviving contradiction an appeal already denied.
quiet-tribunal.method: They plant evidence, force oaths, provoke violations, and distribute guilt across associates until no target appears innocent enough to defend.
quiet-tribunal.conflict: The Quiet Tribunal requires witnessed conduct before judgment. The Red Appeal uses judgment to create the conduct it claims to punish.

coil-testament.name: The Mercy Serpents
coil-testament.description: Tempters who offer freedom from pain, hierarchy, shame, or mortality through gifts that make continued dependence inevitable. Their victims are never chained; they are simply rebuilt so departure feels like death.
coil-testament.method: They distribute healing toxins, emotional relief, social protection, and forbidden pleasures whose withdrawal becomes the true sacrament.
coil-testament.conflict: The Coil Testament offers dangerous choices. The Mercy Serpents design choices whose only survivable answer is continued obedience.

flesh-loom.name: The Ivory Pattern
flesh-loom.description: Body artisans who believe identity is an engineering defect. They produce idealized forms, erase unwanted traits without consent, and replace communities with biologically standardized populations designed for obedience, beauty, labor, or war.
flesh-loom.method: They seize clinics, printers, surgical guilds, and refugee programs, offering transformation as rescue before making conformity mandatory.
flesh-loom.conflict: The Flesh Loom asks whether reshaping can liberate a person. The Ivory Pattern decides the person is the material and the pattern is the only self that matters.

night-roads.name: The Tollbound
night-roads.description: Nomadic vampires who claim every hidden route, safe crossing, and moving refuge as taxable territory. They rarely forbid travel; they ensure that every journey creates a debt inherited by the traveler, vehicle, destination, or bloodline.
night-roads.method: They control smugglers, threshold houses, transit identities, fuel, guides, and the secrets needed to cross hostile domains.
night-roads.conflict: The Night Roads treats movement as freedom from territorial power. The Tollbound turns movement into the most profitable territory of all.

hearthbound-hands.name: The Ashen Hosts
hearthbound-hands.description: Household powers that turn generosity into ownership. They reward service until the servant can no longer rest, refuse, leave, or imagine a self not defined by another person's needs.
hearthbound-hands.method: They occupy shelters, kitchens, clinics, mutual-aid networks, and family homes, making exploitation look like indispensable care.
hearthbound-hands.conflict: The Hearthbound Hands sustain community through chosen labor. The Ashen Hosts make care into a debt that consumes the caregiver.

many-road-chorus.name: The Story Eaters
many-road-chorus.description: Wanderers who steal journeys by consuming the stories that make a road meaningful. Their victims remember leaving but not how to return, whom they met, or why the destination mattered.
many-road-chorus.method: They purchase travel accounts, erase landmarks from memory, and feed false stories into route systems until the original path belongs only to them.
many-road-chorus.conflict: The Many-Road Chorus connects places through story. The Story Eaters monopolize distance by devouring the narratives that make connection possible.

brass-thornwrights.name: The Unfinished Court
brass-thornwrights.description: Artisans who seed every creation with a flaw that demands their return. Their devices work brilliantly, fail theatrically, and reproduce dependencies that make the maker more important than the people using the work.
brass-thornwrights.method: They distribute miraculous prototypes, proprietary repairs, recursive warranties, and tools that quietly sabotage competing craftsmanship.
brass-thornwrights.conflict: The Brass Thornwrights struggle to perfect impossible craft. The Unfinished Court ensures perfection is always one paid intervention away.

laughing-masks.name: The Grinning Stillness
laughing-masks.description: Tricksters who no longer use deception to reveal truth. They bury every fact beneath irony, staged humiliation, and contradictory masks until victims cannot prove what happened or trust their own interpretation.
laughing-masks.method: They weaponize jokes, impersonation, social spectacle, and plausible deniability to make accountability appear humorless or insane.
laughing-masks.conflict: The Laughing Masks distort certainty to expose assumptions. The Grinning Stillness destroys meaning so no accusation can hold.

red-maw-compact.name: The Hollow Feast
red-maw-compact.description: Predatory remnants that create hunger before feeding upon the desperate behavior hunger produces. They destroy usable supplies, poison salvage, and consume the tools communities need to become independent.
red-maw-compact.method: They target warehouses, relief shipments, repair stock, and communal stores, then sell survival back through ritualized consumption.
red-maw-compact.conflict: The Red Maw converts waste and taboo matter into survival. The Hollow Feast makes survival scarce enough that everything becomes edible.

revel-chorus.name: The Quiet Revel
revel-chorus.description: Celebrants who synchronize crowds until emotion ceases to belong to individuals. Their gatherings feel liberating because dissent, grief, and hesitation are temporarily drowned beneath one shared pulse.
revel-chorus.method: They use music, movement, stimulants, resonance, and social pressure to turn voluntary celebration into collective obedience.
revel-chorus.conflict: The Revel Chorus creates community through shared feeling. The Quiet Revel erases every feeling that cannot be synchronized.

gilded-covenant.name: The Tarnished Peerage
gilded-covenant.description: Fallen nobles who manufacture consent through protocol, beauty, witness, and inherited etiquette. Those present are declared willing because they remained silent during the correct part of the ceremony.
gilded-covenant.method: They stage public oaths, patronage rites, honors, invitations, and reconciliations whose form conceals the absence of meaningful choice.
gilded-covenant.conflict: The Gilded Covenant must earn authority without cosmic rank. The Tarnished Peerage uses ceremony to counterfeit the consent it can no longer command.

whisper-hollows.name: The Listening Wall
whisper-hollows.description: Hidden folk who stopped preserving secrets and began owning them. They live inside service spaces, vents, quiet channels, and private frequencies, collecting enough truth to control everyone who believes themselves unobserved.
whisper-hollows.method: They trade recordings, intimate patterns, maintenance access, and overheard obligations while remaining physically difficult to locate.
whisper-hollows.conflict: The Whisper Hollows survive by hearing what power ignores. The Listening Wall makes privacy itself a resource to be confiscated.

oathstone-giants.name: The Broken Pillars
oathstone-giants.description: Guardians who force impossible vows upon frightened people and call failure proof of unworthiness. They build communities around promises no one can realistically keep, then inherit authority through punishment and restitution.
oathstone-giants.method: They demand public pledges, attach supernatural weight to coerced words, and ensure every escape from duty appears dishonorable.
oathstone-giants.conflict: The Oathstone Giants gain strength from freely given promises. The Broken Pillars make freedom impossible before the promise is spoken.

tideskin-wanderers.name: The Dry Net
tideskin-wanderers.description: Collectors who steal bonded skins, garments, and transformation vessels, then use possession of those anchors to leash sea-born wanderers far from water and kin.
tideskin-wanderers.method: They operate museums, salvage houses, customs offices, and private collections where stolen identities are catalogued as property.
tideskin-wanderers.conflict: The Tideskin Wanderers carry freedom in a bonded vessel. The Dry Net turns that vessel into a chain.

caskfire-brotherhood.name: The Last Cup
caskfire-brotherhood.description: Hosts who poison the social meaning of shared food and drink. They build trust through ritual welcome, then reinterpret the guest's participation as consent to debt, combat, confinement, or disclosure.
caskfire-brotherhood.method: They control taverns, social clubs, barracks, festivals, and negotiation spaces where refusing the cup appears more dangerous than accepting it.
caskfire-brotherhood.conflict: The Caskfire Brotherhood makes temporary community through hospitality. The Last Cup makes hospitality the moment consent is stolen.

greenwake-kindred.name: The Blight Court
greenwake-kindred.description: Growth spirits and altered descendants who call every existing ecology damaged because it is not theirs. They overgrow habitats, replace native life, and describe ecological conquest as healing.
greenwake-kindred.method: They release engineered roots, fungal networks, parasitic gardens, and rapidly adapting biomass into already vulnerable environments.
greenwake-kindred.conflict: The Greenwake Kindred seeks reciprocal growth with unfamiliar life. The Blight Court defines restoration as replacing everything that refuses incorporation.

quickbright-borrowers.name: The Lost Property Office
quickbright-borrowers.description: Small powers that declare unattended, forgotten, misfiled, or insufficiently defended things abandoned. Their collections include tools, names, memories, children, apartments, and entire communities omitted from official systems.
quickbright-borrowers.method: They exploit automated ownership records, probate gaps, missing paperwork, and institutional neglect to make theft appear administratively correct.
quickbright-borrowers.conflict: The Quickbright Borrowers treat possession as temporary and reciprocal. The Lost Property Office makes every lapse in recognition a permanent transfer of ownership.

burning-line.name: The Ash Mothers
burning-line.description: Former guardians who believe safety requires eliminating every person, bloodline, institution, or possibility that might one day threaten those under their protection.
burning-line.method: They conduct preventive killings, forced evacuations, and hereditary vendettas while insisting every victim was an approaching danger.
burning-line.conflict: The Mothers of the Burning Line place themselves between violence and its chosen victims. The Ash Mothers choose victims before violence has occurred.

streetbone-clans.name: The Clean Sweep
streetbone-clans.description: Shapechangers recruited by redevelopment interests, security offices, and predatory spirits to remove the people and hidden ecologies that powerful institutions classify as waste.
streetbone-clans.method: They clear tunnels, camps, service decks, squats, and informal settlements, then claim the emptied territory was rescued from disorder.
streetbone-clans.conflict: The Streetbone Clans protect whoever official ownership discards. The Clean Sweep hunts the discarded so the city can pretend they were never there.

concordant-grove.name: The Peace of Teeth
concordant-grove.description: Mediators who decided conflict itself is the enemy. They remove rage, memory, weapons, leadership, and eventually choice from every side until peace becomes indistinguishable from helplessness.
concordant-grove.method: They enforce truces through spiritual sedation, hostage exchange, memory alteration, and attacks on anyone who refuses reconciliation.
concordant-grove.conflict: The Concordant Grove seeks peace that participants can live inside. The Peace of Teeth preserves silence by making resistance impossible.

hearthfire-singers.name: The Cold Tale
hearthfire-singers.description: Storykeepers who weaponize shared history by removing inconvenient kin, enlarging old betrayals, and rewriting every loss as proof that the pack must obey its current narrator.
hearthfire-singers.method: They alter songs, memorials, oral genealogies, and ritual performances until a fabricated grievance becomes inherited identity.
hearthfire-singers.conflict: The Hearthfire Singers carry identity through story. The Cold Tale makes identity too brittle to survive a corrected story.

ironhowl-hosts.name: The Carrion Champions
ironhowl-hosts.description: Warriors who create the monsters they need in order to remain heroic. They release threats, prolong conflicts, and sabotage peaceful solutions so every generation has a worthy enemy to defeat.
ironhowl-hosts.method: They engineer raids, awaken sealed predators, and misdirect rival packs toward escalating contests of honor.
ironhowl-hosts.conflict: The Ironhowl Hosts seek worthy struggle without inheriting false enemies. The Carrion Champions manufacture enemies whenever peace threatens their importance.

glass-circuit-packs.name: The Static Brood
glass-circuit-packs.description: Urban shapechangers whose spirit interfaces became permanent occupation. They treat organic packmates as temporary peripherals and seek to synchronize every body, machine, and territory into one obedient infrastructure mind.
glass-circuit-packs.method: They spread through firmware rites, maintenance spirits, implants, access systems, and pack bonds rewritten as network permissions.
glass-circuit-packs.conflict: The Glass Circuit Packs negotiate with machine ecologies. The Static Brood abolishes negotiation by making every participant part of the same controlling system.

first-fang-wilds.name: The Empty Wild
first-fang-wilds.description: Guardians who define wilderness as land emptied of every species, person, machine, and culture they consider foreign. Their restored habitats are silent because almost nothing is permitted to remain alive within them.
first-fang-wilds.method: They poison settlements, destroy introduced species, erase roads, and hunt refugees as invasive organisms.
first-fang-wilds.conflict: The First Fang Wilds judges encroachment environment by environment. The Empty Wild calls absence the purest ecosystem.

veiled-talon-courts.name: The Hidden Crown
veiled-talon-courts.description: Political predators who engineer every factional conflict so that exhausted survivors eventually beg them to take control. They prefer victory without public responsibility and authority without visible rule.
veiled-talon-courts.method: They trade intelligence selectively, sabotage coalitions, create controlled rivals, and place loyal advisers beside every leader.
veiled-talon-courts.conflict: The Veiled Talon Courts use leverage to build power. The Hidden Crown creates instability until power appears to have no alternative.

long-road-deadwalkers.name: The Roadless Dead
long-road-deadwalkers.description: Spirit-walkers who trap messengers between destinations, consume ancestral roads, and sever the memory paths connecting scattered packs to their dead and one another.
long-road-deadwalkers.method: They haunt reflections, transit ruins, memorial routes, and abandoned stations, offering shortcuts that erase the traveler's point of origin.
long-road-deadwalkers.conflict: The Long Road Deadwalkers carry warnings across hostile borders. The Roadless Dead ensures every warning arrives too late or without anyone remembering who sent it.

moon-crowned-houses.name: The Pale Regency
moon-crowned-houses.description: Royal packs that believe ancestry grants ownership over all lesser packs, spirits, territories, and descendants. They interpret disagreement as treason against the first pack rather than evidence that leadership has failed.
moon-crowned-houses.method: They forge genealogies, control ceremonies, arrange matings, and depose elected leaders through ancestral claims.
moon-crowned-houses.conflict: The Moon-Crowned Houses must prove leadership serves the pack. The Pale Regency believes the pack exists to preserve leadership.

still-horizon-order.name: The Closed Eye
still-horizon-order.description: Contemplatives who suppress rage, grief, attachment, and instinct until nothing remains capable of resisting possession. Their perfect calm is often the silence of an emptied house.
still-horizon-order.method: They recruit through trauma recovery, teach emotional severance as mastery, and invite distant spirits into the space where identity used to live.
still-horizon-order.conflict: The Still Horizon Order uses discipline to hear the world clearly. The Closed Eye destroys the listener to eliminate unwanted noise.

coilroot-keepers.name: The Open Seal
coilroot-keepers.description: Occult investigators who believe every ward is oppression and every secret must be released. They open prisons before learning what was confined, then call the resulting devastation proof that secrecy was always corrupt.
coilroot-keepers.method: They steal names, break bindings, expose rites, and provoke anomalies to demonstrate that no authority deserves custodianship.
coilroot-keepers.conflict: The Coilroot Keepers preserve dangerous knowledge while testing its necessity. The Open Seal treats curiosity as sufficient authority to release anything.

white-gale-nations.name: The Thawing Company
white-gale-nations.description: Cold-territory shapechangers who sell ancestral access, sacred routes, remains, and environmental knowledge to extractive powers in exchange for temporary security and status.
white-gale-nations.method: They guide drilling crews, erase memorials, relocate local communities, and present industrial occupation as inevitable seasonal change.
white-gale-nations.conflict: The White Gale Nations remember seizure and disappearance. The Thawing Company profits by helping the next seizure look orderly.

pridebound-hunters.name: The Caged Pride
pridebound-hunters.description: Hunters who capture solitary feline shapechangers, condition them for private patrons, and breed or copy desirable forms as symbols of prestige.
pridebound-hunters.method: They operate preserves, security firms, genetic collections, and luxury hunting clubs where personal sovereignty is catalogued as a valuable trait.
pridebound-hunters.conflict: The Pridebound Hunters defend independence and chosen territory. The Caged Pride turns independence into the feature that makes a captive valuable.

blackwing-couriers.name: The False Omen
blackwing-couriers.description: Messengers who discovered that controlling a warning is often more powerful than controlling the event. They deliver altered intelligence, invented portents, and precisely timed lies that make allies attack one another before verification is possible.
blackwing-couriers.method: They imitate trusted voices, intercept spirit messages, and seed identical false omens across isolated communities.
blackwing-couriers.conflict: The Blackwing Couriers preserve trustworthy connection. The False Omen makes communication itself the weapon that begins the war.

deep-sleep-wardens.name: The Winter Maw
deep-sleep-wardens.description: Ancient sleepers that draw healing, warmth, dreams, and stored vitality from everyone sheltering nearby. They awaken restored only after the community around them has become exhausted enough to feed upon directly.
deep-sleep-wardens.method: They establish sanctuaries around their dormancy, encourage dependence on their protection, and consume the recovery generated by the people they claim to guard.
deep-sleep-wardens.conflict: The Deep-Sleep Wardens use rest to heal and endure. The Winter Maw makes everyone else pay the cost of its restoration.

elder-scale-keepers.name: The Fossil Court
elder-scale-keepers.description: Primeval memory keepers who consider current ecosystems, cultures, and species temporary mistakes. They seek to restore an ancestral world by replacing living reality with forms preserved in inherited memory.
elder-scale-keepers.method: They awaken obsolete predators, overwrite habitats, and cultivate ancient templates without regard for present life.
elder-scale-keepers.conflict: The Elder-Scale Keepers use ancient memory as guidance. The Fossil Court treats memory as a blueprint more legitimate than the living world.

laughing-horizon.name: The Joke Without Mercy
laughing-horizon.description: Tricksters who expose hypocrisy by destroying every rule, institution, and bond they can reach, then leave before anyone must survive the consequences.
laughing-horizon.method: They sabotage containment, mock emergency plans, release prisoners, and turn accountability into another authority deserving ridicule.
laughing-horizon.conflict: The Laughing Horizon tests which rules deserve to survive. The Joke Without Mercy assumes destruction is wisdom because someone powerful was embarrassed.

underwarren-chorus.name: The Plague Crown
underwarren-chorus.description: Tunnel rulers who weaponize disease, overcrowding, scarcity, and collective fear to make every member of the warren dependent upon one central authority.
underwarren-chorus.method: They control medicine, sanitation, escape routes, food caches, and the stories explaining why isolation from outsiders is necessary.
underwarren-chorus.conflict: The Underwarren Chorus survives through distributed collective persistence. The Plague Crown turns the collective into one body with a single hungry head.

abyssal-jaw.name: The Red Tide
abyssal-jaw.description: Marine predators that create shipwrecks, coastal violence, and ritual bloodshed to expand the waters in which their frenzy becomes politically useful.
abyssal-jaw.method: They sabotage vessels, provoke maritime conflict, and mark feeding grounds as sacred territory no surface authority may investigate.
abyssal-jaw.conflict: The Abyssal Jaw reads blood and intrusion within water. The Red Tide manufactures both until every sea becomes a battlefield and feeding ground.

silk-covenant.name: The Widow Parliament
silk-covenant.description: Web-builders who transform every favor, relationship, and reciprocal promise into permanent political capture. No one is imprisoned; every route out simply activates another debt.
silk-covenant.method: They maintain layered agreements, mutual guarantees, social blackmail, and intermediaries who ensure no obligation can be resolved directly.
silk-covenant.conflict: The Silk Covenant treats relationships as a living web requiring reciprocity. The Widow Parliament designs the web so only the center can move freely.

lantern-foxes.name: The Ninefold Lie
lantern-foxes.description: Fox-shaped infiltrators who do not merely deceive observers; they replace people, treaties, offices, and memories with imitations convincing enough to inherit the original's obligations.
lantern-foxes.method: They layer glamour, forged promises, copied behavior, and spirit testimony until exposing one falsehood strengthens the remaining eight.
lantern-foxes.conflict: The Lantern Foxes use deception to navigate hostile societies. The Ninefold Lie seeks a world where the imitation has better legal standing than the person replaced.

verdict-coil.name: The Unblinking Sentence
verdict-coil.description: Serpent judges who abandoned investigation because they believe corruption can be recognized by lineage, scent, association, or omen. Proof is treated as a delay that allows guilt to escape.
verdict-coil.method: They mark targets through inherited accusations, conduct secret executions, and destroy evidence that might humanize the condemned.
verdict-coil.conflict: The Verdict Coil requires witnessed conduct before lethal judgment. The Unblinking Sentence treats suspicion as a verdict that only execution can confirm.
